headline: Soil excavation suspended under Padma Bridge Rail Link over safety concerns
summary: Authorities in Narayanganj have halted soil removal beneath bridge pillars after residents raised alarms over potential structural risks.
details: Authorities in Narayanganj have suspended the extraction of soil beneath the pillars of the Padma Bridge Rail Link at Fatullah’s Aliganj. The work was halted following safety concerns and a lack of prior approval from local administration.

The issue came to light after residents obstructed the activity and videos of the site went viral on social media. Locals claimed that soil had been excavated for days, creating large pits up to 15 feet deep between pillars 84 and 91.

Residents expressed fear that water accumulating in these excavated areas could pose a risk to the bridge structure. The Narayanganj district administration stated they were not informed in advance, which is standard procedure for such operations.

A railway project official explained that the land was previously low-lying and had been filled during construction. He stated that the contractor is now carrying out restoration work to return the site to its original condition as per contract requirements.

Additional Chief Engineer (Track and Works) Abu Yousuf Mohammad Shamim noted that consultants from the Bangladesh Army are supervising the work to ensure safety standards. He suggested the contractor may have hired a third party for the excavation.

The project is being implemented by China Railway Group Limited, with a completion deadline of June 2027. The matter has now been referred to the ministry for a final decision after the administration requested proper documentation.
